text:
Testing is a vital part of software development. It helps teams build reliable applications and avoid frustration later on. At the most basic level, unit tests check individual pieces of code, like a single function, to ensure they work correctly in isolation. Integration tests, on the other hand, check that different parts of the software work well together as a whole.

Many developers use test-driven development, or TDD, where you write a failing test first, then write the minimum code needed to make it pass. This approach guides the design and keeps the code clear. Above all, a solid testing strategy gives developers confidence. Knowing that tests cover the main functions, they can change or improve the code without constant fear of breaking something important.
